title: Broadwater et al. v. Chesapeake Presbytery
summary: Presbytery empowered a commission both to assume original jurisdiction over matters involving church members and to receive a Session's reference concerning a membership transfer. The SJC vacated the original-jurisdiction mandate because Presbytery had neither found that the Session refused to act nor required the commission to make that finding before proceeding. The authority to receive the reference remained intact; requests from other Sessions alone did not satisfy BCO 33-1.

evidence_notes: This is a complaint about Presbytery's commission mandate, not an original-jurisdiction request to the SJC.
The original-jurisdiction portion was vacated; the reference portion expressly stood.
The decisive defect was absence of a finding or required determination that the Session refused to act in a case of process.
